hook: Hyderabad CP warns banks of *AI-assisted* cyber attacks
hook_b: Hyderabad CP warns banks of *AI-assisted* cyber attacks
tldr: Hyderabad CP VC Sajjanar urged banks to tighten security after I4C and CERT-In warned of AI-assisted attacks on financial systems.

beats.what: Sajjanar said third-party software handling confidential data should be secured like core banking apps.
beats.why: I4C flagged 'multi-crore unauthorised transactions' through fund disbursement systems and APIs.
beats.care: Stolen money is routed through mule accounts via IMPS and NEFT, per the advisory.

event.label: CP urges banks to harden security

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Siasat: attackers exploit unpatched software and misconfigured servers, then delete transaction records to hide traces.

cards.q: How confident are you that your bank app is secure?

qs: Will customers be told if their bank is hit?
Who checks third-party apps that banks plug into?

facts.t: Banks and NBFCs must also report incidents to RBI's *DAKSH* portal within 6 hours.
Agencies told banks to follow CERT-In's *May 2026* blueprint on AI-assisted exploits.

viz.l: How the attack works, per I4C

steps.e: AI agents target fund disbursement APIs

viz.verdict: Risk to bank customers' money and data
Risk to bank customers' money and data

learn.t: Mule account = a bank account used to receive and pass on stolen money, often rented from someone else.

watch: Whether banks issue customer alerts after the I4C and CERT-In advisory.

sources.name: Siasat
sources.title: Hyderabad Commissioner warns banks against AI-assisted cyber attacks

fact: Agencies say AI agents are draining banks through *payment APIs* at machine speed.
twist: Banks, NBFCs and fintechs must now report such attacks to CERT-In within *6 hours*.
